Every tool in the Comma package, one page each. Pick a group below, or use the sidebar and the search box.
Getting startedInstall the package and find the tools in Tekla. Model pluginsSection cutting, Boolean clean-up, rebar inspection, model export and import, and the licence manager. Model Edit toolsTwelve tools that fit, align, project, cut, split and swap existing objects. Drawing pluginsMarks, dimension sets, graphical controls and view arrangement for Tekla drawings. Rebar toolsBorder, chairs, shear links, welded mesh, starter bars, punching and opening reinforcement. Report / template propertyA custom property that turns a part’s class into a value for reports and templates. MacrosOne-click macros for modeling and drawing mode.

uRebarEndMarkerPlaces associative notes on the ends of visible reinforcement bars in a drawing — one note per end, independently switchable. uRebarLayerMarkerPlaces a layer symbol on rebar based on its class, using up to 16 configurable class-list → symbol slots (8 shown under a “Top” tab, 8 under “Bottom” — a… uDimensionSetSpacerSpaces out picked dimension sets so they no longer overlap. uGraphicalControlAssigns rebar orientation/scale UDAs (used for graphical bar control) to bars matching a Mark search text. uViewArrangerAligns and distributes the selected drawing views — select two or more views on a sheet first, then click an align or distribute button; each button acts… uSectionMarkAlignerLines up the ends of section marks you have already selected in the active drawing, renames them, and can number them in reading order. The dialog stays open…

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → uDimensionSetSpacer Spaces out picked dimension sets so they no longer overlap.
Option What it does Distance How far apart to space the picked dimension sets (default 5).

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → uGraphicalControl Assigns rebar orientation/scale UDAs (used for graphical bar control) to bars matching a Mark search text.
Option What it does Bar rotation By local axis, By view, or By global Z — how the bar’s graphical control reads its rotation. Bar scale type Yes/No — whether the bar’s graphical control scales with the view. Mark search A wildcard search on Mark, to target only the bars you mean (leave blank to affect all visible bars).

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → uRebarEndMarker Places associative notes on the ends of visible reinforcement bars in a drawing — one note per end, independently switchable.
Option What it does Note 1 / Note 2 Turns the note on/off at each end of the bar, and which note file to use for it. Offset (dX/dY) Shared distance/perpendicular offset applied to both notes — the sign at each end is worked out automatically from the bar’s own geometry. Delete existing Removes any end notes this plugin already placed before adding new ones, so re-running doesn’t stack duplicates. Mirror Auto (recommended — reads the bar’s own shape, safe for a mixed batch of straight and bent bars), Same side, or Symmetric. Place on hook tip On (default): on a bar end that has a hook, the note starts from the tip of the hook. Off: it starts from the end of the bar’s main body, where the hook’s bend begins. Ends without a hook are the same either way. The offsets and the side each note takes are always worked out from the main body, so switching this only moves the starting point.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → uRebarLayerMarker Places a layer symbol on rebar based on its class, using up to 16 configurable class-list → symbol slots (8 shown under a “Top” tab, 8 under “Bottom” — a presentation split: all 16 are evaluated together, the Top rows before the Bottom rows, first match wins). That covers up to eight layers per face.
Option What it does Class list 1–16 Which rebar classes each slot matches (wildcards supported, e.g. 11*). Symbol file / index Which symbol library and symbol to draw for a matching bar. Height / Colour / Position / Offset / Rotation Shared appearance for all the slots in a tab (Top or Bottom). Delete existing Removes any markers this plugin already placed before adding new ones.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → uSectionMarkAligner (also on the Drawing ribbon tab, Section Marks) Lines up the ends of section marks you have already selected in the active drawing, renames them, and can number them in reading order. The dialog stays open, so another group is just select, then click again.
How to use:
Select one or more section marks with Tekla’s own selection tool (box, Ctrl+click). Click Align left end or Align right end, then pick a point in the drawing. The chosen end of each selected section line moves along the line to line up with the picked point. Esc cancels. Use the Section name box with + and - to rename the selected marks, or type a name and press Enter. Option What it does Align left / right end Left and right are Tekla’s own names for the two ends of the mark, not screen directions. Only horizontal and vertical section lines are supported; any other mark is skipped and counted in the status line. Marks in different views are each measured in their own view. Section name, + and - Counts the last run of digits or letters in the name up or down by one (A to B, 9 to 10, A1 to A2, 008 to 009). Words such as Section cannot be counted; nothing is renamed then. Enter in the box gives the marks exactly the typed text. Follow selection On (default): the box shows the name of the selected mark. Off: the box holds the next name to hand out, and + / - name the marks with it and then count the box. Resequence on align Off by default. On: after every Align the selected marks are also numbered in reading order on the sheet (top row first, left to right inside a row), starting from the name in the box and counting from it. Marks within 1 mm of height of the first mark of a row are one row, measured from the end you just aligned, so marks of different line lengths still line up. It runs on the whole selection, only when two or more marks are selected; if the name cannot be counted far enough nothing is renamed and the status line says so. The status line under the buttons reports what was done and what was skipped. The Help link at the top opens this guide.
How counting works: only the last run of digits or letters in the name is counted; everything before it stays as typed. Going up:
1, 2, 3 … 9, 10 (zero-padded names keep their width: 008, 009, 010) A, B, C … Z, AA, AB … (lower case works the same: a, b, c) A1, A2, A3 … A9, A10 1A, 1B, 1C … 1Z, 1AA A-A, A-B, A-C … and SEC 3, SEC 4 Going down is the exact reverse and stops at the first value (A, or 0); numbers never go negative. Not counters: words and mixed case such as Section, letter runs longer than three (ABCD), and names that do not end in a letter or digit (A-). With Follow selection on, + and - refuse these and rename nothing; with it off, the name is still given to the marks and the box stays as typed.
With Follow selection on and several marks selected, the box shows their name only when they all have the same one; otherwise, and when nothing is selected, the box is left as it is. With Follow selection off, for example: type 1, select a mark, click +; the mark is named 1 and the box shows 2.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → uViewArranger Aligns and distributes the selected drawing views — select two or more views on a sheet first, then click an align or distribute button; each button acts immediately, there is no separate Apply step.
Option What it does Align Left / Center / Right / Top / Middle / Bottom Snaps every selected view to that edge (or centre line) of the selection’s own bounding box. Distribute Horizontally / Vertically Spaces the selected views out evenly along that axis, using whichever spacing mode is set below. Use restriction box Off (default): each view’s own frame is used for alignment/spacing. On: its restriction box is used instead. Spacing mode Equal gaps (default, no value needed): even gaps between views. Fixed gap: an exact gap size, entered in the value box. Fixed pitch: an exact centre-to-centre spacing, entered in the value box.

Installing CommaEvery tool documented on this page ships together in a single file, CommaTs.tsep — one install gives you every plugin below, both macro libraries, the Comma… How to use this documentPlugins live in Tekla under Applications & Components (Ctrl+F), under the Comma group. Every plugin also has its own button on a dedicated Comma ribbon tab…

Plugins live in Tekla under Applications & Components (Ctrl+F), under the Comma group. Every plugin also has its own button on a dedicated Comma ribbon tab (Modeling and Drawing modes each have one) — no need to open the catalog every time. The twelve Model Edit tools sit together in a two-row group at the right of the Modeling tab. Macros live in the same catalog, under Comma > Macros — split into Modeling and Drawing tabs depending on which mode you’re in. Macros are catalog-only, not on the ribbon. Every plugin dialog shows a licence status in the top-right corner (Licensed / License expired / Trial days remaining / Trial expired). If it reads License expired, paste your renewed key into uCommaLicenseManager and click Activate.

Every tool documented on this page ships together in a single file, CommaTs.tsep — one install gives you every plugin below, both macro libraries, the Comma ribbon tab, and the custom property, rather than installing each one separately.
To install: double-click CommaTs.tsep — Tekla’s own extension installer takes it from there and puts every file where Tekla expects it. No manual copying. Supported versions: Tekla Structures 2024.0 and newer. Current version: 26.1.33. uCustomProperty is the one exception: this package includes the Tekla 2026 version only. A site still on Tekla 2024 needs uCustomProperty2024 installed separately — see its own entry below. Licence: each computer gets a 45-day trial the first time a Comma tool runs on it, with nothing to register. To keep working after that, request a licence key for the computer:
In Tekla open Applications & Components (Ctrl+F), group Comma, and run uCommaLicenseManager. It shows this computer’s Machine ID and the current licence or trial status. Click Request a license, enter the email address the key should be sent to and click Submit request. If your mail app opens, press Send there. When the key arrives, paste it into the License key box and click Activate. The same status (Licensed / License expired / Trial days remaining / Trial expired) shows in the top-right corner of every plugin dialog. Details are in the uCommaLicenseManager entry.

Applications & Components → Comma → Macros, Drawing tab.
uSwitchDimensionTag Select a dimension set and run this repeatedly to cycle its tag position through all 7 positions (left/right upper/middle/lower, plus the per-span middle-lower tag) — one step forward each time.
uAddMarkUsingAppliedProperties Adds a mark to the current view using Tekla’s “applied properties” mark command.
uAlignHorizontal / uAlignVertical Aligns the active view horizontally or vertically — the same as Tekla’s own native align-view commands, available as a one-click macro.
uCreateRebarSetDimensions Adds rebar-set dimension marks to the selected views (or every relevant view, if none are selected) for every reinforcement set group found there.
uFreeplaceAnnotations Switches every annotation object (marks, dimensions, symbols — anything that isn’t a view or a model object) in the selected/all views to free placement and rearranges them automatically.
uFreeplaceArrangeDrawing Switches every view on the sheet to free placement and re-arranges the whole drawing layout.
uMoveMarksHorizontalToPerpendicular / uMoveMarksVerticalToPerpendicular Select one or more marks, then run this to reposition them horizontally or vertically so their leader line reads perpendicular, accounting for the view’s own leader-line-extension setting.
uOpenPhaseManager Opens Tekla’s Phase Manager dialog directly to the Phases tab.
uOpenProjectUDA Same macro as the Modeling-tab one above — opens the Project UDA dialog straight to Classification, available here too since it’s useful from a drawing as well.

data.uhideselected#\u003cimg class=\"tool-ico:
Applications & Components → Comma → Macros, Modeling tab. Select the object(s) first, then run the macro — macros act on the current selection rather than prompting you to pick.
uReverseRebar Reverses the picked shape/range of a selected rebar object — flips a SingleRebar’s polygon point order, a RebarGroup/CurvedRebarGroup/CircleRebarGroup/RebarMesh’s start/end direction. Select exactly one object, then run.
uReverseHook Reverses the hook direction (negates the hook angle) on the start and end hooks of the selected rebar object(s) — works on SingleRebar, RebarGroup, CurvedRebarGroup, CircleRebarGroup, RebarSet, and RebarMesh, and accepts a multi-object selection.
uOpenProjectUDA Opens the Project user-defined attributes dialog and jumps straight to the Classification field. No selection needed. (The same macro is also available in Drawing mode — see below.)
uShowOnlySelected Hides everything except the selected objects. Hold Shift while running it to show the other objects as transparent instead of hiding them.
uHideSelected The opposite of uShowOnlySelected: hides exactly the selected objects, completely (no reference line left), and leaves everything else visible. Selecting an assembly or component hides everything in it. Hold Shift to make them transparent instead of hidden. Redraw the view to show them again.

data:
Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit, and the two-row Model Edit group on the Comma ribbon tab. Twelve tools that edit the geometry of existing objects. They share one rhythm: set the options in the dialog, click Apply, pick a reference, then pick the targets (or preselect them before you click Apply); the command repeats until Esc. Gap fields accept arithmetic such as (2+3)*4 and imperial feet/inch fractions, according to XS_IMPERIAL_INPUT when the dialog opens.
Each change is a native Tekla modify: if an error stops a run, earlier changes can remain, so inspect the model and use Undo before retrying. These tools are new in this release: try them on a copy of your model first. uFitFits beam ends, plate edges, control lines and rebar ends to a picked reference: a face, a plane, or a line. Set the reference and gap, pick the reference… uAlignMakes beams, plates, bolt arrays, control lines and more parallel (or perpendicular) to a picked face, plane or line, without changing their length. uProjectorProjects objects onto a face, a plane, a point on the work plane, or a line, either moving them or creating copies. uCutCreates native plane cuts on parts, from a face, a three-point plane, a line, or a line through two points. uFitPlateFits ContourPlate edges and manual BentPlate leg edges to a face, a three-point plane or a line. uFittingCreates a native end fitting on straight beams, so the beam is trimmed or extended to the reference without moving its stored endpoints. uCutoutCuts one object out of others: pick a Beam or ContourPlate as the cutter, then the parts to cut. uSplitSplits ContourPlates, Beams and ControlLines at a point, a line, or a plane. uCombinePlateMerges contour plates: the first selected plate is kept and the second is removed after a checked merge. uSplitPlateSplits contour plates into replacement plates: the source plate is replaced after the outputs and assembly have been checked. This is separate from Split… uExtenderSplits and extends physical straight beams against a group of reference beams. uSwapReverses the direction (the handles) of selected objects. It does not exchange the locations of two objects.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → uAlign (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit group) Makes beams, plates, bolt arrays, control lines and more parallel (or perpendicular) to a picked face, plane or line, without changing their length.
How to use:
Choose Reference (Face, Plane 3 points or Line) and Orientation (Parallel or Perpendicular), or tick Rotate only. Click Apply, pick the reference, then pick the targets if none were preselected. Finish with the middle mouse button. Repeat until Esc. Option What it does Reference Face, Plane 3 points or Line. Orientation Parallel or Perpendicular to the reference. Rotate only Keeps the primary axis and only rotates about it. Needs a face or plane reference. Plane references support Beam, PolyBeam, ContourPlate, BoltArray and ControlLine (parallel plane also supports Connection, Detail and Weld). Line references support Beam, BoltArray and ControlLine. Rotate only supports Beam, PolyBeam and BoltArray. Anything else is reported as unsupported.
Rebar: a SingleRebar or polygonal RebarGroup turns rigidly about its first input point, so its hooks and the distribution of a group turn with it. Parallel and Perpendicular aim the first leg of the bar by the smallest rotation (the roll is carried along), for face, plane and line references. Rotate only rolls a planar bent bar about its first leg; a straight or non-planar bar has no roll to set and is skipped. After the turn the physical bars, hooks included, are read back and must sit where the rotation predicts; otherwise the bar is turned back and listed. Component-owned bars, RebarSet bars, bars with child objects and spiral or curved groups are skipped and listed, and a RebarSet itself is not supported yet. Each bar turns about its own first point, so bars selected together with a beam do not follow that beam’s rotation.
A native failure stops the batch; earlier changes can remain, so inspect the model and use Undo before retrying. More details:
PolyBeam uses its own-axis rotation for both plane orientation labels, matching the reference behavior. BooleanPart and other bolt layouts have no reference dispatch and are reported as unsupported. Failed work-plane restoration is reported as an uncertain state. Standard attributes load on opening. Negative reference mode selects the first reference; RotateOnly and Orientation normalize to No/Yes and Parallel/Perpendicular. Perpendicular is authoritative over contradictory legacy Parallel flags. Normalized attributes apply without starting a model operation.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → uCombinePlate (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit group) Merges contour plates: the first selected plate is kept and the second is removed after a checked merge.
How to use:
Select the contour plates in order, then click Apply. Extra selections are combined one pair at a time. Pick a new plate when one remains; Esc ends. The original chamfers are replaced by the evaluated polygon vertices (with no chamfer).
If a write fails, the command stops and reports possible partial changes; inspect and Undo before retrying. A failure while cleaning up the operative objects can leave objects that need inspection. More details:
Additional selections form a pair queue. Operative cleanup failures can leave objects requiring inspection.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → uCut (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit group) Creates native plane cuts on parts, from a face, a three-point plane, a line, or a line through two points.
How to use:
Optionally select the target parts, then click Apply. Pick the reference: a Face, exactly three Plane points, a Line, or two Line points. Pick the target parts if none were preselected. With Remove: Pick side, pick a point on the side to remove. The command repeats until Esc. Option What it does Reference Face, Plane 3 points (pick exactly three points), Line, or Line 2 points. Line references support beams only. Gap Signed, in mm. A plane gap follows the picked normal; a line gap follows each beam’s center/axis side. Remove Smaller or Bigger choose the side by the part’s center of gravity (not by comparing resulting volumes); Pick side uses your point. Perpendicular Cuts beams across their local X direction, using profile/OBB candidates and the nearest-end gap rule. Other part types in Face/Plane mode keep the reference plane. Existing cuts and fittings are retained. Apply uses the current settings and restarts the command; the Gap list keeps the last five applied values.
More details:
Gap is signed in millimetres. Line gap follows the per-beam center/axis-side normal with the reference rule’s negative sign. Smaller and Bigger choose a side using the part’s center of gravity; these options do not compare resulting volumes. The editable Gap list retains five applied values in this process. Apply restarts through Tekla’s command mechanism. A new request waits for the previous native pick to return before it runs.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → uCutout (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit group) Cuts one object out of others: pick a Beam or ContourPlate as the cutter, then the parts to cut.
How to use:
Pick the cutter (a Beam or ContourPlate), then the target parts. Set the gaps and the branch options in the dialog before you click Apply. Option What it does Name Name given to the created cutout. Side gap, End gap Metric numbers or arithmetic expressions (for example (2+3)*4), or imperial feet/inch fractions per XS_IMPERIAL_INPUT when the dialog opens. Blank becomes zero; invalid input blocks Apply. Convex hull, Interpolation, High accuracy Choose how the cutter outline is built where applicable. Standard attributes load on opening: gaps with an absolute value above 9999 mm reset to 0 and negative flags reset to 0. Opening the dialog does not start a model operation.
More details:
Four typed branches support gaps, convex hull, interpolation and high accuracy where applicable. Side/End gaps follow XS_IMPERIAL_INPUT when the dialog opens: metric numbers or arithmetic expressions (for example (2+3)*4), imperial feet/inch fractions. Reopen the dialog after changing input units. Standard attributes load on opening: gaps with absolute value above 9999 mm reset to 0; negative flags reset to 0. After an error, inspect possible partial changes and use Undo before retrying.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → uExtender (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit group) Splits and extends physical straight beams against a group of reference beams.
How to use:
Choose Beam or OBB, a signed Gap and a Minimum length, and tick Split and/or Extend. With Pick two groups, pick the reference beams, finish the pick, then pick the beams to edit. Otherwise pick one group: the first beam’s direction defines the references. Click Apply; picking repeats until Esc. Option What it does Extension mode Beam, or OBB (OBB mode can create a fitting for oblique intersections). Gap May be negative. Arithmetic expressions are accepted, in Tekla input units. Minimum length Pieces shorter than this are removed. The cleanup runs last, even when Split and Extend are off. Split, Extend Split runs first; Extend then processes both selected ends in sequence. Fitting Create fittings for oblique intersections (OBB mode). Assembly Add split pieces joins the clones to the original assembly when the source is a secondary part. Clones of a main part stay separate. If no beam has split stations, the original targets go on to Extend and cleanup. In a mixed group only the split outputs advance; beams without stations stay in the model and are left out of the later stages. Component-owned beams, bolts, welds, reinforcement and unsupported children are blocked.
A failure can leave verified or partial changes: inspect the model and use Undo before retrying. More details:
Otherwise pick one group; the first beam direction defines references, including opposite directions within the audited angular threshold. One-group preselection is used for the first operation only. Clones of a main part remain separate, matching MPD Edit. In mixed groups, only split outputs advance: beams without stations remain in the model and are excluded from later stages. Existing Fitting/CutPlane children use checked snapshots. Empty or reversed split plans are also blocked. Comma startup choices are Beam, Extend on, two groups, Split/Fitting/AddToAssembly off, Gap and Minimum length zero.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → uFit (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit group) Fits beam ends, plate edges, control lines and rebar ends to a picked reference: a face, a plane, or a line. Set the reference and gap, pick the reference, then pick the objects to fit.
How to use:
Choose Reference (Face, Plane 3 points (pick exactly three points), Line, or Line 2 points.) and a Gap, or preselect the objects before you click Apply. Click Apply, pick the reference, then pick the objects to fit if none were preselected. Finish a multiple pick with the middle mouse button. The command repeats until you press Esc. Option What it does Reference Face, Plane 3 points (pick exactly three points), Line, or Line 2 points. Gap Signed, in mm. Shifts the plane along its normal (reversing the point order of a 3-point plane reverses the normal). The Gap list remembers the last five applied values while Tekla runs. Beam OBB For beams, uses the part’s oriented bounding box to choose the projected candidate instead of the raw handle. Supports beam endpoints and height, PANEL PolyBeam height, ordinary PolyBeam endpoints (not with a Line reference), ControlLine endpoints, bolt group positions, ContourPlate edges and BentPlate legs. ContourPlate and BentPlate fitting keep the surviving contour points and chamfers; picked-edge options for plates are in uFitPlate.
Rebar: SingleRebar and polygonal RebarGroup, with a Face or Plane reference only. The end whose input point is nearer the plane moves along its end leg onto the plane (Gap shifts the plane). Only input points move: hooks, end offsets and bend radii stay as they are, so the physical bar end stays short of the plane by the bar’s end offset (a 4 mm end offset ends 4 mm before the plane); use Gap to compensate. Bars owned by a component, bars generated by a RebarSet, bars with child objects, and spiral or curved groups are skipped and listed. A one-polygon group is also skipped when its bar ends are not parallel to the plane, because only the defining bar would reach it.
Rebar sets: pick the set or any bar it generated and uFit edits the set, never the generated bars. The leg face edge the bars end on moves onto the plane (Gap shifts the plane), the set regenerates and every bar follows; a slanted plane puts each bar end on the slanted line. Hooks, spacing and the other edges stay as they are. At the fitted edge the bars end exactly on the plane: a set made from its host drops its end inset there (tested: 32 mm became 0), so use Gap if you want cover. If a set keeps an end inset at that edge, the fit is undone and the report names the inset. A set is skipped and listed when its bars end on more than one leg face edge or leg face, when a bar ends outside its leg face, when the plane is parallel to the leg face, when the fit would fold a bar, and when a component owns the set. The result is read back after the change and the leg face is restored if a bar does not end where the geometry predicts. This edits the leg face of the set, so check it against the host.
For a beam parallel to the reference plane the height branch changes the profile to a rectangle (height × width), which can replace an I, U, L or M profile. Check profiles after fitting such beams. More details:
Fit modifies Beam endpoints/height, PANEL PolyBeam height/contour translation, ControlLine endpoints and the input points at the ends of SingleRebar and polygonal RebarGroup. Face, Plane through three points, native Line and Line through two points are available. Pick a reference, then targets, or preselect targets before launching. Beam Line fitting converts Gap by the angle to the stored endpoint axis. Beam OBB uses section bounds to choose a projected candidate; ControlLine ignores that option. Plane/ControlLine ties edit Start/Point1; Beam Line ties edit End. ContourPlate supports all four reference modes with gap, default seed selection, sequential individual-edge fitting and two post-fit cleanup passes. Surviving contour point identities/chamfers are retained. BentPlate Face/Plane uses automatic free-edge group selection; Line/Line2Points selects a current free edge independently for each manual leg. Both use sequential leg fitting, with checked whole-geometry Modify/restoration. BentPlate uses the fixed MPD Fit mean-distance strategy and minimize behavior. Advanced picked-edge options belong to Fit Plate. For a Beam parallel to the reference plane, the height branch changes the profile to height*width and may translate both endpoints. This can convert the profile shape to a rectangle, including I/U/L/M profiles. Apply saves attributes and starts a new command; The Gap list keeps the last five applied values. PolyBeam Type PANEL supports Face/Plane height fitting: rectangular profile and conditional translation of every contour point. Ordinary PolyBeam types support Face/Plane endpoint fitting; all PolyBeam Line modes are unsupported by the MPD Edit 2.00.2 reference command and are reported without changes. Ordinary PolyBeam fitting uses raw first/last contour segments, ignoring OBB and retaining chamfers. Two nearly parallel segments (0.08 radians) are skipped. Collapsed segments are rejected. BoltGroup Plane fitting offsets the plane once and edits the nearest First/SecondPosition (tie First). Line fitting uses the closest point on the bolt axis and direct axial Gap (tie Second), without Beam angle conversion. OBB is ignored. Check the pattern, attached parts and holes after fitting. Selected BooleanPart resolves its current operative Part. Operative Beam uses the Beam adapters; operative ContourPlate supports all four references through the same checked writer; operative BentPlate uses the same four reference modes and checked writer. The BooleanPart and operative share an ID; edits retain Father and operation type. Plate Line builds a target plane through the reference line using the plate normal. Gap shifts that plane along LineDirection cross PlateNormal; reversing the line reverses the positive Gap side. Beam angle conversion and OBB do not apply to plate Line. A line parallel to the plate normal cannot define the target plane and is reported before mutation. Rebar supports Face and Plane references only (Line references are reported without changes). The end whose input point is nearer the plane moves along its end leg onto the plane, with Gap shifting the plane; ties edit the first point. Gap supports metric arithmetic or imperial feet/inch fractions according to XS_IMPERIAL_INPUT at dialog opening. Blank retains the prior gap. Invalid input blocks Apply; history displays matching units. Reopen after unit changes. On opening, standard attributes load and normalize: absolute Gap above 1e9 mm becomes 0, negative Mode selects the first reference, UseObb normalizes to No/Yes. Normalized attributes apply without starting a model operation.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → uFitPlate (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit group) Fits ContourPlate edges and manual BentPlate leg edges to a face, a three-point plane or a line.
How to use:
Select the plates, choose the reference, and set the options. Click Apply, pick the reference, then pick an edge when Edge selection is set to pick one. Repeat until Esc. Option What it does Reference Face, Plane 3 points (pick exactly three points), Line, or Line 2 points. Gap Signed, in mm. Metric or imperial per XS_IMPERIAL_INPUT when the dialog opens; blank keeps the last gap. Edge selection Automatic, or Pick edge (a native line pick). Side Nearest keeps the contour side closest to the reference; Farthest keeps the opposite side. Minimize/Maximize chooses between the fitted top and bottom surface areas. Fit all Controls picked-line matches and multi-leg ambiguity. For an automatic BentPlate Plane fit, Yes selects independently on each current leg; No selects one global group. Automatic ContourPlate and automatic BentPlate Line fits ignore it. The last five applied gaps are kept for this tool during the current Tekla session.
More details:
Gap is signed in millimetres. Fit all controls picked-line matches and multi-leg ambiguity. Gap accepts metric arithmetic or imperial feet/inch fractions according to XS_IMPERIAL_INPUT at dialog opening. Reopen after changing units. Standard attributes are loaded and normalized on opening.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → uFitting (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit group) Creates a native end fitting on straight beams, so the beam is trimmed or extended to the reference without moving its stored endpoints.
How to use:
Select the target beams before you start, or pick them after the reference. Choose Face, Plane 3 points, Line or Line 2 points. For a plane pick exactly three points and finish; for two points use the native line preview. Enter Gap and click Apply. Repeat until Esc. Option What it does Gap (Face, Plane) A positive gap shifts along the picked plane normal; reversing the point order reverses that normal. Gap (Line) A separate plane is calculated for each beam. A positive gap moves toward its current fitted center and a negative one away from it. Reversing the picked line or the beam axis does not change this rule. Parallel lines and references with no defined beam-center side are skipped, and the reference face’s own part is excluded from the targets. Existing cuts and fittings are preserved.
More details:
Existing cuts and fittings are preserved by this build. The editable Gap list remembers the last five applied values for this tool while Tekla is running.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → uProjector (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit group) Projects objects onto a face, a plane, a point on the work plane, or a line, either moving them or creating copies.
How to use:
Select the targets first, or pick them after the reference. Choose the options and click Apply. Pick the reference: a face, a three-point plane, a point through the current work plane, or a line. Repeat until Esc. Option What it does Reference Face, Plane 3 points, point through the work plane, or Line. Direction How the projection runs onto the reference. Alignment For beams: Keep original, Align to plane, Align by OBB, OBB above/below plane, or Project nearest point. Action Move modifies the targets; Copy creates new objects. Project nearest point modifies the original beam even with Copy selected. Gap Signed, in mm. Metric arithmetic or imperial feet/inch fractions, according to XS_IMPERIAL_INPUT when the dialog opens. Blank keeps the previous gap. Line mode skips PolyBeam, ControlPolycurve and rebar targets, and a ControlPolycurve Move is refused before any other target is changed.
After an error some changes may remain: use Undo as needed. Rebar: a SingleRebar or polygonal RebarGroup is projected like a plate: every input point of the bar, and the distribution points of a group, moves onto the plane along the chosen Direction (Gap shifts the plane). Move edits the bar; Copy duplicates it with all its attributes and user attributes and projects the copy. Hooks, end offsets and bend radii are not changed, and the beam-only Alignment options do not apply. Rebar can be preselected or picked after the reference. The picker takes parts and rebar; any other picked object is ignored and listed in a message. Rebar never blocks the other targets of a selection. A bar is skipped, and listed in a message after the run, when a leg runs along the projection direction (it would collapse), when a bend would fold flat, when the projection would change the distribution length or the distance between the polygons of a group (a spacing-based group would gain or lose bars), when the direction is parallel to the plane, in Line mode, and for component-owned bars, RebarSet bars, bars with child objects and spiral or curved groups; a RebarSet, mesh or strand is not supported. A bar that already lies on the plane is skipped silently, for Copy too. Every Move and Copy is read back; a Move that fails the read-back is put back and listed.
More details:
Blank retains the prior gap. Invalid input blocks Apply; history displays the same units. Reopen after unit changes. On opening, standard attributes load and normalize: absolute Gap above 1e9 mm becomes 0, negative indices become first option and Action becomes Move/Copy. Normalized attributes apply without starting a model operation.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → uSplit (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit group) Splits ContourPlates, Beams and ControlLines at a point, a line, or a plane.
How to use:
Select the targets, choose a reference mode and click Apply. Press Esc to end picking. Point: pick the split location (for a plate, the dividing plane is perpendicular to its local X axis). Line / Line 2 points: define the reference line. Face: use a picked face plane for plates and beams (ControlLines stay unchanged). Plane 3 points: define a plane with three non-collinear points. Parallel work plane: pick the location of the parallel plane. Option What it does Reference Point, Line, Line 2 points, Face, Plane 3 points, or Parallel work plane. Minimum length Removes Beam pieces shorter than this length (pieces exactly at the minimum are kept). Metric or imperial per XS_IMPERIAL_INPUT; blank becomes zero, invalid input blocks Apply. Multi mode Continues with the retained selection until Esc. Plate line references define a dividing line on the plate surface; Face/Plane references must cross it. Both plate pieces are kept. Plate cuts with Beam/ContourPlate operative geometry are preserved; additive Booleans and other cutter types are rejected before splitting. ControlLines need at least 1 mm from each end and the longer half keeps the original identity. PolyBeam splitting is not available. Check bolts, welds and assembly ownership after splitting.
More details:
Additive Booleans and other cutter types need separate support and are rejected before splitting. Minimum length removes Beam pieces shorter than the entered length. Minimum length follows XS_IMPERIAL_INPUT when the dialog opens: metric numbers or arithmetic expressions (for example (2+3)*4), or imperial feet/inch fractions. Reopen the dialog after changing input units. PolyBeam splitting is inactive in the MPD 2.00.2 reference.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → uSplitPlate (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit group) Splits contour plates into replacement plates: the source plate is replaced after the outputs and assembly have been checked. This is separate from Split (which cuts in place).
How to use:
Select the contour plates, then choose a reference. Point uses the nearest plate edge to establish a perpendicular split line. Line and Line 2 points project the picked line onto the plate surface. The command repeats until Esc; Apply starts a new pick session. Option What it does Reference Point, Line or Line 2 points. A projected corner, or a line outside the plate, leaves the plate unchanged. Gap Signed separation: positive separates the new plates, zero meets at the reference, negative overlaps them. Assembly Add to assembly keeps the original assembly; when the source was its main plate, the first replacement becomes main. Unsupported attachments and cutter types are blocked before the source plate is deleted.
On a partial failure, inspect the reported state and use native Undo before retrying. More details:
Gap is signed separation: positive separates the new plates, zero meets at the reference, negative overlaps them. It creates replacement plates and deletes the source after output and assembly checks succeed.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → uSwap (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit group) Reverses the direction (the handles) of selected objects. It does not exchange the locations of two objects.
How to use:
Choose which families to include in the dialog (a selection limit of 0 means unlimited) and click Apply. Preselected objects are used once; after that you pick interactively. Finish each selection to reverse its handles. Esc ends the command. Option What it does Families Beams, Polybeams, Plates, Bolts, Construction objects, Reinforcement and Items. Selection limit Largest number of objects per run; 0 = unlimited. Swap only reverses the handles and never changes the profile. A symmetric profile keeps its exact solid; an asymmetric profile (for example an HZ sheet pile) is reversed anyway, but its solid is then not the mirror of the original, and a warning appears under the prompt line with the object ID and profile — check those objects.
Reinforcement: planar SingleRebar and open polygonal RebarGroup are reversed with their hooks, bend-radius order, group end covers and distribution. Item (Brep) parts are reversed like beams. Bolt arrays, RebarSet, mesh and strand targets are skipped and listed even when their family is ticked.
The whole selection is prepared and checked before any write. Objects Swap cannot reverse (unsupported types, non-BEAM native subtypes, deformed parts, component-owned objects) are left unchanged and listed after the run. Select hosts and their reinforcement or bolts in separate runs.
After a native failure partial changes can remain: inspect the reported object and use Undo. More details:
The whole enabled selection is prepared and checked before any writes. An object Swap cannot reverse (no writer for its type yet, or a refused safety gate) is left unchanged and listed after the run; every other object is reversed. Select hosts and their reinforcement or bolts in separate runs; related targets in one selection are rejected before writes. Beam offset/Position compensation and catalog reflection checks protect physical placement. An asymmetric profile (for example HZ sheet piles) is reversed anyway, but its solid is then not the mirror of the original: a warning appears under the prompt line with the object ID and profile, so check those objects. All recorded phase, typed UDAs, attachment and assembly checks must remain valid. Directionally ambiguous source chains or groups are rejected before any write. For rebar groups, Rebar groups: bar shape reverses the bars of each group and Rebar groups: range reverses the pick line of a normal group (its first bar becomes its last); switch on either or both. Range changes nothing else, so an uneven spacing, exclusion or cover is mirrored, exactly as if the range had been picked the other way round. Tapered, spiral, tapered-curved and circle groups are skipped for range and listed after the run. Item (Brep) parts are reversed like beams: start and end points swap, Position and point offsets are compensated, and the profile is kept; if the item’s shape is not verified symmetric a warning is shown. Bolt arrays, RebarSet, Mesh and Strand targets are skipped and listed until their writers are added, even when their family checkbox is enabled.

uSectionCutterCuts a section line/plane through picked parts and draws the resulting intersection. Runs as a one-shot tool: click it once, then keep picking — it stays open… uRemoveBoolsStrips Boolean operations from picked parts — the fastest way to “un-cut” a part without hunting down each individual cutting part by hand. Five independent… uRebarInspectorOne dialog for the shape and the hooks of selected reinforcement: read a bar into a sketch, edit its points, legs, angles and hooks, then apply the result to… uExportImportMoves a model between Tekla versions through an XML file: export it here, then open a new, empty model in the other version and import the same file there. uRebarClassDecoderTwo modes, picked from the Mode dropdown at the top of the dialog. Both work the same way otherwise: run on whatever is selected in the model, or on the entire… uCommaLicenseManagerManages the Comma licence for this machine — shows the Machine ID (with a Copy button), current licence/trial status, and lets you activate a licence key. No…

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → uCommaLicenseManager Manages the Comma licence for this machine — shows the Machine ID (with a Copy button), current licence/trial status, and lets you activate a licence key. No drawing or model needs to be open to use it.
Getting a licence: click Request a license, enter the email the key should be sent to (name, company, number of computers and a note are optional) and click Submit request. This computer’s Machine ID is filled in for you. Submitting sends the request to the Comma license desk. The desk also gets an email with the same details, and we reply to the address you enter with your key. If the server cannot send that email, or the request cannot reach the license desk (no internet, a blocked proxy), your mail app opens instead: press Send there so we receive the request. Paste the key you receive into the License key box and click Activate.
When a licence has passed its expiry date the status reads License expired and Activate is available again — paste the renewed key and click Activate; there is no need to Remove the old one first.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → uExportImport Moves a model between Tekla versions through an XML file: export it here, then open a new, empty model in the other version and import the same file there.
How to use:
Export: choose the file, optionally tick Selected objects only, and press Export. A selection also takes what it hangs on. Import: open a new, empty model in the target version, choose the same file and press Import. Import UDAs controls whether user-defined attributes are read back. Import adds everything in the file to the open model, so importing into a model that already has the objects creates them twice. Carried across: parts and items, cuts, fittings, bolts, welds, surface treatments, grids, reinforcement and rebar sets. Reinforcement whose part cannot be rebuilt gets a DUMMY part instead. Stop cancels a running export or import.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Rebar → uRebarClassDecoder (also on the Comma ribbon tab) Two modes, picked from the Mode dropdown at the top of the dialog. Both work the same way otherwise: run on whatever is selected in the model, or on the entire model.
Mode What it does Decode: Class → UDAs Reads each object’s own Class (must already be set, as a 4-digit code) and writes N_BAR_LAYER, N_BAR_DIRECTION and N_BAR_CONDITION from it. Compile: UDAs → Class The reverse — reads N_BAR_LAYER, N_BAR_DIRECTION and N_BAR_CONDITION and writes Class from them. A UDA that was never set counts as Other (OTH, digit 9), so a bar with none of the three set compiles to 9999. Class code reference. Open Class code reference in the dialog to see what each digit of the code means — layer name, layer number, direction and pour condition, from the firm’s MT-M-02.3 rule sheet — with worked examples and a box that decodes any 4-digit code you type. The whole one-page sheet, which also covers part classification and the bridge part names, opens from Classification rule (PDF) at the top right of the dialog. It is installed with the plugin, so it works without the network or the firm folder.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Rebar → uRebarInspector One dialog for the shape and the hooks of selected reinforcement: read a bar into a sketch, edit its points, legs, angles and hooks, then apply the result to the model. It replaces the former uRebarShapeTools and uRebarHookTools.
How to use:
Select reinforcement in the model. The dialog always follows the Tekla selection; switch Hold the view on to keep the bars shown now whatever you select in Tekla. The reload button (circular arrow) reads the bars again: from the model when the view is held, from the Tekla selection otherwise; bars with unapplied sketch edits are kept. The pin button keeps the window on top of Tekla; the gear opens the settings. Every control has a tooltip. Click a point, a leg or a hook in the sketch and edit its values in the panel. Drag a point to slide it along a leg (10 mm steps, Shift for 1 mm). Double-click selects and zooms in Tekla. Tick Preview sketch in model to see the edited polygon, with leg lengths and hook tails, as temporary graphics in the active view. Press Apply to model to write it, or Revert to drop unapplied edits. Option What it does Dimensions Length (L1 / Ln) and angle of the selected leg. Keep angles on: changing a leg moves the rest of the bar along, so no other angle changes. Off: only that leg’s end point moves. Hooks Angle (90°, 135°, 180°) and tail length (mm or × d) of the start and end hooks. Reverse turns each hook to the other side: the angle is negated and the hook becomes a custom hook. Shape Reverse the point order, Offset every point along the plane normal, or Flatten every point onto the plane. The plane is fitted automatically (best fit) or defined by picking 3 points. Standards Checks every bend radius and hook against the reinforcement catalog (rebar_database.inp) row for the bar’s grade, size and usage: the minimum bend radius, and the radius and length of the 90°, 135° and 180° hooks. A bend below the minimum, or a custom hook that differs from the catalog, turns the bar’s status in the list to a warning. Correct to catalog sets the flagged bend radii and hook radii/lengths to the catalog values. Under Settings (the gear) the switches choose which of bend radii, hook radii and hook lengths are corrected, Keep larger bends (on by default) leaves radii above the minimum alone, and Catalog usage Auto takes tie/stirrup for a closed bar and main otherwise. In the bars list, invalid bars (Tekla reports weight 0) are red, shapes Tekla does not recognise (its own recognition says UNKNOWN, or the SHAPE code from your rebar shape rules is UNKNOWN or 99) brown, bars longer than the limit under Settings (default 12 m) teal, bend radius problems purple, hook problems orange and off-plane points blue; the list is grouped in that order and the Show drop-down at the top limits the list to one kind. Rebar sets are read-only, so they are left out of the list (the status line says how many). The weight and shape warnings can be turned off in Settings, and a longest bar of 0 turns the length warning off. Hooks that use a standard 90/135/180 shape already follow the catalog. A tapered group is checked on its first polygon. Range Reverse range for rebar groups. Spacing, exclude and offsets stay in Tekla’s own rebar dialog. Several bars at once The bars list takes Ctrl/Shift-click. With two or more rows selected the footer switches to Selected, so one press of the operation (for example Correct to catalog) runs on exactly those bars. Right-click: Select all in this group picks every bar of a group (for example all the Bend radius ones); Skip in “All that fit” marks special bars (a bar with a deliberate radius) so All that fit leaves them out for the rest of the session, and Include again undoes it. Selected always runs on what is selected, skipped or not. Re-pick points Picks the polygon again in Tekla, with Tekla’s own snapping.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → uRemoveBools Strips Boolean operations from picked parts — the fastest way to “un-cut” a part without hunting down each individual cutting part by hand. Five independent switches decide exactly what gets removed.
How to use:
Click the icon in the catalog. Switch on whichever of the five operation types below you want removed (Boolean cuts/adds/weld preps are on by default; cut planes and fittings are off by default). Pick the parts to clean up (several at once is fine — pick, then confirm). Every enabled operation type on those parts is removed immediately. Picking repeats until Esc. Option What it does Cut planes Off by default. A CutPlane object — a plane cut that can never extend a part’s own boundaries (different from a Boolean cut). Fittings Off by default. A Fitting object — a plane fit that can make a part longer or shorter, not just cut it. Boolean cuts On by default. A Boolean part whose Type is Cut. Boolean adds On by default. A Boolean part whose Type is Add. Weld preps On by default. A Boolean part whose Type is Weld prep.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → uSectionCutter Cuts a section line/plane through picked parts and draws the resulting intersection. Runs as a one-shot tool: click it once, then keep picking — it stays open until you press Esc.
How to use:
Click the icon in the catalog (or press Apply from its dialog). Choose a Mode: Line + Z (pick 2 points, cuts vertically through the active view’s own orientation), Plane (3 points) (pick 3 points directly), or Face (pick a face on a part — its own plane is used). Line + Z and Plane mode both show a live grey line following the cursor while picking, the same rubber-band preview Tekla’s own native commands use — Face mode does not (it picks a face directly, not points). Pick the parts to cut (you can pick several at once, then confirm). The cut repeats immediately for another line/plane/face — press Esc when done. Option What it does Offset Shifts the cutting plane along its own normal before intersecting (0 = exactly as picked). Line color Colour of the drawn cut lines (construction-object mode only). Line type Solid / Dashed / Slashed / Dash dotted / Dotted (construction-object mode only — a reference DXF has no line-type table, so that mode always exports a continuous line regardless of this setting). Add points Also marks every vertex of the cut with a construction point. Orient to XY Off by default (cut geometry stays at its real 3D model location). On: re-orients the cross-section into the cutting plane’s own local 2D coordinates and moves it to the global origin (0,0,0) on the XY plane — useful for pulling a cross-section out to look at flat, on its own, instead of wherever in 3D it was actually cut. Applies to both Creation methods below. Note: every cut made with this on lands at the same origin, so repeated cuts will overlap there rather than spread out through the model. Creation method Construction object (default): the cut is inserted as plain construction lines/points, same as the native “Add construction line” tool. Reference DXF: the same cut geometry is written to a small DXF file and inserted as a reference model instead — useful if you want the result to sit in its own toggleable layer rather than mixed in with ordinary construction objects. The DXF file is saved in a uSectionCutter subfolder inside the model’s own folder, one file per cut. Note: Line + Z mode follows the active view's orientation, not a work plane set via the Cpl command — for a plane that follows a custom work plane, use Plane (3 points) mode instead.

uBorderRebarPlaces a border reinforcement set on a slab or wall opening edge in the families U, S, L1/L2, Q1/Q2 and Z1/Z2. Pick the input part and three points; the dialog… uChairsRebarPlaces chairs (bar supports) under a reinforcement mat. The leg and offset fields are measured to the outside of the bars, so a typed leg length is the length… uShearLinksRebarPlaces shear links (stirrups) in a beam or column, with hook-plane and standard-hook handling matched to Tekla’s own hooks. Leg lengths are outside dimensions… uWeldedMeshRebarPlaces welded mesh (rebar mesh and mesh groups) on a slab, with cross-bar placement checked against Tekla’s own mesh orientation. In vertical mode the top and… uStarterBarsRebarPlaces starter bars for a wall from the foundation or slab, in nine bar types (ss, se, l1, l2, q1, q2, z1, u1, u2) with spacing rules shared with the Border… uPunchingRebarPlaces punching-shear reinforcement around a column in fifteen layouts (central, external and corner, five variants each). Items are rebar groups, rebar… uOpeningRebarPlaces the reinforcement around a circular or rectangular opening in a slab: trimmers, stub and cut-mesh bars, and for the typical circular detail four tangent… Upgrading from the earlier Clone buildsOnly installations that ran the earlier “Clone” builds of the seven rebar tools are affected. The official build drops the Clone suffix from the Tekla plugin…

Only installations that ran the earlier “Clone” builds of the seven rebar tools are affected. The official build drops the Clone suffix from the Tekla plugin strings (u<Name>RebarClone becomes u<Name>Rebar). A component placed by an earlier build may therefore not be recognised by the tools of this build: re-place it, or keep the earlier build for that model. Check on a copy of the model first.
A saved dialog set is named after its dialog, which is now u<Name>Rebar.MainWindow. Drag your model, project and firm folders onto extensions\RebarPresetMigration\Migrate-RebarPresets.cmd to copy the sets saved as <set>.u<Name>RebarClone.MainWindow.xml to the new names. Nothing is overwritten and the old files stay; add -WhatIf first to see what would be copied.
Remove the old folders u<Name>RebarClone, uRebarShapeTools and uRebarHookTools from the extensions folder before installing the package.

data:
Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Rebar → uBorderRebar Places a border reinforcement set on a slab or wall opening edge in the families U, S, L1/L2, Q1/Q2 and Z1/Z2. Pick the input part and three points; the dialog writes the bars as rebar groups or single bars, checked against the bar spacing rules in the shared spacing library. Leg lengths, widths and covers are outside dimensions. The dialog has 183 fields; the tool passes its native suite (5423 checks) and an end-to-end insert and modify test on Tekla 2026.
The Tekla plugin string is uBorderRebar. Components placed by the earlier Clone builds (uBorderRebarClone) may not be recognised by it; see Upgrading from the earlier Clone builds. Sets saved under the earlier dialog name are carried over with the preset migration helper.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Rebar → uChairsRebar Places chairs (bar supports) under a reinforcement mat. The leg and offset fields are measured to the outside of the bars, so a typed leg length is the length you get on the bar. Defaults: a B500B 12 bar with 50 mm covers. The tool passes its native suite (4053 checks) and an end-to-end insert and modify test on Tekla 2026.
The Tekla plugin string is uChairsRebar. Components placed by the earlier Clone builds (uChairsRebarClone) may not be recognised by it; see Upgrading from the earlier Clone builds. Sets saved under the earlier dialog name are carried over with the preset migration helper.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Rebar → uOpeningRebar Places the reinforcement around a circular or rectangular opening in a slab: trimmers, stub and cut-mesh bars, and for the typical circular detail four tangent diagonals and four corner bars along the bisectors, with a clash check against the other bars. It reuses the Border engine for its sides, and the covers of the bar families stack in layers from the face cover. The tool passes its native suite (5882 assertions) and end-to-end insert tests on Tekla 2026; the typical-detail dialog tab is not yet tested in Tekla.
The Tekla plugin string is uOpeningRebar. Components placed by the earlier Clone builds (uOpeningRebarClone) may not be recognised by it; see Upgrading from the earlier Clone builds. Sets saved under the earlier dialog name are carried over with the preset migration helper.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Rebar → uPunchingRebar Places punching-shear reinforcement around a column in fifteen layouts (central, external and corner, five variants each). Items are rebar groups, rebar meshes, or stud-rail embeds. Defaults are the standard set shipped with the package. For rebar groups and meshes the cover, height and overhangs are bar-surface and outside dimensions. The tool passes its native suite (18692 checks) on Tekla 2026; the dialog’s Modify, Get and Save/Load paths are not yet tested in Tekla.
The Tekla plugin string is uPunchingRebar. Components placed by the earlier Clone builds (uPunchingRebarClone) may not be recognised by it; see Upgrading from the earlier Clone builds. Sets saved under the earlier dialog name are carried over with the preset migration helper.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Rebar → uShearLinksRebar Places shear links (stirrups) in a beam or column, with hook-plane and standard-hook handling matched to Tekla’s own hooks. Leg lengths are outside dimensions and the start and end offsets are bar-surface covers. The tool passes its native suite (3490 checks) and an end-to-end insert and modify test on Tekla 2026.
The Tekla plugin string is uShearLinksRebar. Components placed by the earlier Clone builds (uShearLinksRebarClone) may not be recognised by it; see Upgrading from the earlier Clone builds. Sets saved under the earlier dialog name are carried over with the preset migration helper.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Rebar → uStarterBarsRebar Places starter bars for a wall from the foundation or slab, in nine bar types (ss, se, l1, l2, q1, q2, z1, u1, u2) with spacing rules shared with the Border tool. Bars that cannot be spaced as a group fall back to single bars. Foot, hook and U-leg lengths are outside dimensions. The tool passes its native suite (4062 checks) and an end-to-end insert and modify test on Tekla 2026.
The Tekla plugin string is uStarterBarsRebar. Components placed by the earlier Clone builds (uStarterBarsRebarClone) may not be recognised by it; see Upgrading from the earlier Clone builds. Sets saved under the earlier dialog name are carried over with the preset migration helper.

Where to find it: Applications & Components → Comma → Rebar → uWeldedMeshRebar Places welded mesh (rebar mesh and mesh groups) on a slab, with cross-bar placement checked against Tekla’s own mesh orientation. In vertical mode the top and bottom covers are bar-surface covers and the cross-bar overhang is measured past the outer face of the longitudinal bar. The tool passes its native suite (3133 checks) and an end-to-end insert and modify test for groups and meshes on Tekla 2026.
The Tekla plugin string is uWeldedMeshRebar. Components placed by the earlier Clone builds (uWeldedMeshRebarClone) may not be recognised by it; see Upgrading from the earlier Clone builds. Sets saved under the earlier dialog name are carried over with the preset migration helper.
uCustomPropertyNot a tool you click — a computed value you reference from a Template Editor field or a report/BOM column, typed as CUSTOM.CLASS\_BASED. It reads a part’s own…

Where to find it: Not in the catalog — referenced by name from a report or Template Editor field Not a tool you click — a computed value you reference from a Template Editor field or a report/BOM column, typed as CUSTOM.CLASS_BASED. It reads a part’s own Class and returns a computed value, usable in an integer, double, or character field alike. This is expected to grow more custom properties over time, not just this one.
Two versions ship: uCustomProperty for Tekla 2026, and uCustomProperty2024 for Tekla 2024 and 2025. If CUSTOM.CLASS_BASED does not evaluate after installing uCustomProperty on a Tekla 2025 machine, install uCustomProperty2024 there instead.
